subject: Dedicated sizing: multi-profile session mix for NovaCorp pilot
messages:
From: James Lane <jlane@novacorp.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing input for pilot rollout

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. We’re scoping a dedicated-reserved pilot with Redwood to serve an enterprise assistant across our customer base. Quick profile below — we’re trying to get a 'ballpark for committed capacity' to feed procurement and execs this week. Any back-of-envelope numbers are fine; we know we’ll refine after you get more telemetry.

High-level profile:
- Traffic: steady-state ~200 requests/sec (rps), peak bursts to ~800 rps during rollouts and daytime spikes.
- Session behaviour: average session = 1.7 requests, median inter-request gap ~25s, 12% sessions are multi-turn (>5 turns).
- Prompt/response lengths: prompt avg 120 tokens, response avg 420 tokens (distribution: 55% short <250 tokens, 35% medium 250-700, 10% long >700).
- Call type: 88% sync (blocking UI), 12% async/background jobs.
- P95 latency target: 250ms; p99 soft target: 600ms (we can accept graceful degradation beyond p99).
- Models: prefer open-family 70B variants; interested in quantized options if you can keep p95 SLA.
- Security: enterprise data, strict audit; we’ll need Private/DEDicated option and bring-your-own-VPC eventually.

File: I attached a small CSV export of token histograms and a short spike trace for last 72 hours.

Questions for you: what inputs do you need to make an initial reserved-GPU recommendation? Can you provide a simple 1-page mutual action plan we can share with procurement? Also, timing: we’re hoping for a pilot commit within 30 days.

Thanks,
James Lane
Head of AI Platform | NovaCorp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: James Lane <jlane@novacorp.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-11-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing input for pilot rollout

Hi James — thanks, this is a great start. Looping in Ben and Vivek for an initial capacity sketch. I attached a short template (capacity_input.xlsx) — if you can fill the shaded fields it will let us do a more defensible estimate.

Immediate clarifying items (quick answers OK):
- Can you share percent traffic per endpoint (assistant.compose, assistant.revise, search.rerank)? A split helps us map to model context lengths.
- Token breakdown by endpoint vs. by daypart (peak vs. off-peak) — if not available, an approximate fraction is fine.
- How tolerant is the UX to p99 degradation? Example: is 1s p99 acceptable for <5% of requests during bursts?
- Are there any features that require persistent KV-cached sessions (i.e., long-term state per user) vs ephemeral requests?
- Any regulatory constraints on model residency or quantization (some FSI customers prohibit external export of raw activations)?

Next steps:
1) Ben/Vivek will produce a 1–2 option capacity sketch (cost vs latency tradeoffs) by EOD tomorrow.
2) We’ll produce a mutual action plan + sample SOW for pilot commitment (template attached).

Attachments: capacity_input.xlsx (spreadsheet) — please upload your filled file to the Drive link below when ready.

HubSpot: I linked this thread to DEAL-7342 so procurement visibility is captured.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-11-13T08:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing input for pilot rollout

Marissa — quick back-of-envelope before we get the filled template from NovaCorp. Assumptions pulled from James’ note: 800 rps peak, avg tokens/request = prompt(120)+response(420)=540 tokens.

Compute math (rough):
- Peak token rate = 800 rps * 540 tokens = 432,000 tokens/sec.
- Typical throughput we budget in reserved GPU terms depends heavily on model+quantization. For a quantized 70B (Q4_K/M style) on high-memory GPUs we often budget ~6k–18k tokens/sec per GPU depending on BSP and batch size; to be conservative I’ll use 12k tokens/sec/GPU for mixed-length interactive workload.
- Capacity estimate (conservative) = 432,000 / 12,000 ≈ 36 GPUs. If we use more aggressive quantized kernels or H100-class hardware we can reduce that to ~18–24 GPUs.

Latency vs cost tradeoffs:
- Option A (latency-optimized): 36 x A100/H100 equiv dedicated, aggressive batching disabled for sync calls, p95 <250ms at peak. Higher cost but meets SLA.
- Option B (cost-optimized): 20–24 x H100-grade with autoscaling headroom + prefix caching; accepts graceful p99 bump for <5% of peak. Saves ~30% list-cost.
- Option C (hybrid model routing): route simple /short endpoints to smaller quantized 13–33B models running on dense hosts, keep 70B pool for long responses — reduces 70B footprint to ~10–14 GPUs and uses an additional 8–12 smaller-GPU nodes for short/fast traffic.

Other notes:
- KV cache/session affinity: if NovaCorp requires persistent KV per user for long sessions, we must size memory footprint and avoid too much oversubscription — would add ~10–15% GPU headroom.
- Burst sizing: recommend burst quota that allows up to 2x baseline for 5–10 minutes with pre-warmed standby instances; this mitigates rollout spikes.

I’ll draft a 1-page sketch and accompanying cost delta table for the three options and send back to Marissa and Vivek by EOD. We’ll also surface expected reserve-term pricing (monthly commit) vs on-demand.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Pre-Sales Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated sizing input for pilot rollout — Redwood sketch and next steps

Hi James — forwarding our internal sketch. Attached is a concise estimate (redwood-dedicated-estimate-DEAL-7342.pdf) that lays out three capacity options, expected monthly commit bands, and a short mutual action plan for pilot sign-off. Highlights below:

- Recommended starting point: Option C (hybrid routing) — reduces 70B GPU count from ~36 down to ~12–14 by routing short endpoints to smaller models. Expected to meet 95th latency target and reduce cost materially for interactive UI flows.
- Burst plan: standby pool (pre-warmed) sized to absorb 1.5–2x baseline for 10 minutes; we’d require a short warm-up window for very large bursts.
- Pilot timeline: we can have a pilot cluster provisioned within 10 business days after the signed pilot SOW + purchase order.
- Next actions for NovaCorp: complete the attached capacity_input.xlsx with endpoint splits and the daypart CSV; confirm the acceptable p99 degradation threshold and any quantization constraints.

Links: upload the completed spreadsheet to the Drive link in the related_links list, or reply with the file directly. I’ll set up a 30-minute sizing review with Ben & Vivek tomorrow morning if that works.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
